les: Hoe ons weet hoe hulle geleef het
kaps_punt: Hoe ons inligting van jagter-versamelaars en herders verkry: Stories, Voorwerpe, Rotstekeninge, Boeke, Tans (Vir die huidige sal ons oor hulle uitvind deur die waarneming van die lewende samelewings - etnografie)

items.bewering: Die jagter-versamelaars en herders het nie boeke geskryf of foto's geneem nie.
items.bron: Oral tradition, no written records among the San: Cambridge (Africa journal), 'Three nineteenth-century southern African San myths'; UCT Digital Bleek and Lloyd (lloydbleekcollection.cs.uct.ac.za): San narratives survive in writing only because Bleek and Lloyd recorded them from 1870. Photography did not exist before contact. Volledige nagaan, eerste rondte.

items.bewering: Historici en argeoloë gebruik daarom ander leidrade, wat ons bronne noem.
items.bron: UCLA History, 'Primary & Secondary Sources' (history.ucla.edu); Wikipedia 'Historical source': historians and archaeologists work from sources such as artefacts, oral testimony and documents.

items.bewering: Party stories is oor baie geslagte heen oorvertel, van ouers na kinders.
items.bron: San knowledge passed from generation to generation through songs and stories, with versions changing in the retelling: Cambridge, 'Three nineteenth-century southern African San myths: a study in meaning' (Africa); Cambridge, 'Structure, Meaning and Ritual in the Narratives of the Southern San'. No source names parents specifically, but 'van ouers na kinders' is the ordinary sense of handing something down the generations.

items.bewering: Die stories vertel onder meer van diere en van wat mense geglo het.
items.bron: UCT Digital Bleek and Lloyd: the /Xam notebooks hold narratives and descriptions of 'rituals, beliefs and customs'; Cambridge (Africa) San myths study: stories of /Kaggen (mantis, eland) and other animal beings.

items.bewering: Voorwerpe (artefakte) is dinge wat mense self gemaak of verander het om te gebruik.
items.bron: Oxford Department for Continuing Education, ArchaeOx fact sheet 'Artefacts' (archeox.conted.ox.ac.uk); New World Encyclopedia 'Artifact (archaeology)': an object made or modified by people.

items.bewering: Argeoloë vind dit in die grond en in rotsskuilings.
items.bron: Kuhlase and Forssman, 'Ostrich eggshell beads from Little Muck Shelter', Southern African Field Archaeology (journals.uj.ac.za); Stewart et al., beads excavated from the Sehonghong and Melikane rock shelters, Lesotho (Science News).

items.bewering: Klipgereedskap en krale van volstruiseierdop wys hoe mense gewerk en hulself versier het.
items.bron: Southern African Field Archaeology (journals.uj.ac.za), Little Muck Shelter: Later Stone Age ostrich-eggshell beads used as personal ornaments, drilled with microlithic stone drills; Science News on the hunter-gatherer ostrich-eggshell bead exchange network.

items.bewering: Rotskuns of rotstekeninge is kuns wat mense op rotse geskilder of in die klip ingekerf het.
items.bron: Wits Rock Art Research Institute, 'Hunter-gatherer rock arts of Africa' (wits.ac.za/rockart): paintings in caves and rock shelters, engravings (petroglyphs) on rock outcrops of the interior plateau; SAHO, Driekopseiland rock engravings: made by scratching and pecking the rock surface.

items.bewering: Baie daarvan is prente van mense wat jag en dans. Party prente wys ook dinge wat die mense geglo het.
items.bron: Wits Rock Art Research Institute, 'Hunter-gatherer rock arts of Africa': researchers once thought the art was 'simply a record of daily life or a primitive form of hunting magic', a view now rejected; the art centres on the trance dance and the spirit-world experiences of San ritual specialists. Anne Solomon, 'Rock Art in Southern Africa', Scientific American (January 2005): 'hunting scenes in rock art are not as common as early researchers believed'; 'rock art can best be understood as a religious art', not 'reflections of everyday concerns'. Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography' (G. Blundell): eland the most commonly painted animal in most areas, alongside 'ubiquitous depictions of healing or trance dances'. Wits RARI: on the engravings, animals appear more often than people.
items.regstelling: Each sentence is defensible on its own, but together they teach the view researchers have dropped: that the art mostly shows everyday life such as hunting, with belief added in 'some' pictures. Hunting scenes are not common, animals (especially the eland) are among the most common subjects, and most researchers now read most of the art as being about belief. Dance is right: the healing or trance dance is a very common subject. Keep the dance, drop hunting as a main subject, name animals, and make belief the main meaning rather than an extra. In substance: many pictures show animals such as the eland, and people dancing, and researchers think much of the art has to do with what the people believed.

items.bewering: Baie later het mense van elders die San en Khoikhoi ontmoet en oor hulle geskryf.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Bartolomeu Dias reaches present Mossel Bay' (3 February 1488) and the Bartolomeu Dias Museum: first recorded contact between Khoekhoen and European seafarers; SAHO, 'Early struggles: contact and conflict in the Cape Colony' (Saldanha 1503, Van Riebeeck's journal); Anne Good, Journal of Early Modern History, on more than 100 travel narratives after 1719. Rock art and oral tradition are thousands of years older (Wits RARI), so 'baie later' holds.

items.bewering: Party het ook die San se stories neergeskryf.
items.bron: UCT, The Digital Bleek and Lloyd (lloydbleekcollection.cs.uct.ac.za): Wilhelm Bleek and Lucy Lloyd wrote down /Xam narratives from 1870; the collection was entered in UNESCO's Memory of the World Register in 1997.

items.bewering: Elke boek wys hoe sy skrywer die mense gesien het.
items.bron: Anne Good, Journal of Early Modern History: European narratives about the Khoikhoi were shaped by prejudice; Siegfried Huigen, 'Knowledge and Colonialism' (hosted by SAHO); Nigel Penn, 'Written culture and the Cape Khoikhoi': Kolb is an important but contested source.

items.bewering: Navorsers leer ook deur mense wat vandag leef dop te hou en met hulle te praat. Hierdie soort navorsing noem ons etnografie.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Ethnography': the systematic study of cultures through participant observation and interviews; Social Research Glossary (qualityresearchinternational.com). The Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography' uses the term this way for San research.

items.bewering: Leefwyses verander met die tyd, dus wys hierdie navorsing nie presies hoe mense destyds geleef het nie.
items.bron: The Kalahari Debate (Wilmsen; Lee and Guenther; Barnard 2006), summarised in Wikipedia 'Kalahari Debate'; 2017 Journal of Anthropological Archaeology study of the Ju/'hoansi and !Xoo: complex changes from 1850 to the present behind apparent continuity. Present-day ethnography is not a direct window on the past.

items.bewering: Elke bron is net een leidraad, en saam vertel hulle ons die meeste.
items.bron: Superlative ('die meeste') checked as a methodological claim, not a ranking of facts: historians read every source critically for its author and purpose and combine several (UCLA History, 'Primary & Secondary Sources'); Wits RARI and Mazel (Bradshaw Foundation) on how rock art interpretation advanced by combining the art with 19th- and 20th-century ethnography. It holds as stated.

items.bewering: bronne: Dinge soos foto's, geskrifte, stories, onderhoude en voorwerpe wat ons iets van vandag en van lank gelede vertel.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Primary source' and 'Historical source'; UCLA History: photographs, written documents, oral history interviews and artefacts are all sources. The list after 'soos' is open, and 'van vandag' does not contradict the block's statement that hunter-gatherers took no photographs.

items.bewering: leidraad: Iets wat jou help om die antwoord op 'n vraag uit te vind.
items.bron: Plain meaning of 'leidraad' (clue), consistent with how historical method treats sources as evidence (UCLA History). No factual risk.

items.bewering: historikus: Iemand wat bronne bestudeer om die verlede te verstaan en te beskryf.
items.bron: UCLA History, 'Primary & Secondary Sources'; Wikipedia 'Historical source': historians study and interpret sources to reconstruct the past.

items.bewering: argeoloog: Iemand wat dinge van lank gelede soek en ondersoek om uit te vind hoe mense geleef het.
items.bron: ArchaeOx fact sheet 'Artefacts' (Oxford); excavation reports in Southern African Field Archaeology (Little Muck Shelter): archaeologists recover and analyse material remains to understand past human life.

items.bewering: artefak: 'n Voorwerp wat mense self gemaak of verander het.
items.bron: ArchaeOx fact sheet 'Artefacts' (Oxford); New World Encyclopedia 'Artifact (archaeology)': made or modified by humans. Natural objects used unchanged are ecofacts or manuports, which the 'gemaak of verander' wording correctly leaves out.

items.bewering: rotskuns: Kuns wat mense op klip verf of in die klip inkap.
items.bron: Wits RARI, 'Hunter-gatherer rock arts of Africa': paintings and engravings; SAHO, Driekopseiland: engravings made by pecking and scratching. 'Inkap' (pecking) and the study block's 'ingekerf' (incising) are both real engraving techniques, so the two blocks do not disagree.

items.bewering: etnografie: Navorsing waarin iemand mense dophou en met hulle praat om te leer hoe hulle leef.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Ethnography'; Scribbr, 'What is ethnography?': participant observation plus interviews or conversations, to understand a group's way of life.

opsomming: One claim is contradicted: the rock-art block says much of the art shows people hunting and dancing, with belief in only 'some' pictures, which is the older view researchers (Wits Rock Art Research Institute; Solomon, Scientific American 2005) have dropped: hunting scenes are not common, animals such as the eland are central, and most of the art is read as being about belief; the dance is right. Everything else, including the definitions, the books on the San and Khoikhoi, Bleek and Lloyd and the ethnography caveat, checks out.
